name: Vega
tagline: The former and future North Star — astronomy's zero-point of brightness.

facts.label: Debris disk
facts.value: Yes — early evidence of planetary systems

history: Vega is the fifth-brightest star and the anchor of the astronomical magnitude scale — by convention its brightness defined zero. Earth's axis wobbles over a 26,000-year precession cycle, which made Vega the pole star around 12,000 BCE and will crown it again near 13,700 CE. It was the first star ever photographed (1850) and the first outside the Sun to have its spectrum recorded. In 1983 the IRAS satellite found Vega radiating far more infrared than a bare star should — a ring of cold dust, one of the first clues that planetary systems are common.
